verses.1:1: An oracle of the word of the Lord concerning Israel by the hand of His messenger: Lay it now upon your hearts.
verses.1:2: "I have loved you," says the Lord. "Yet you said, 'In what way have You loved us?' Was not Esau Jacob's brother?" says the Lord. "Yet I loved Jacob,
verses.1:3: but Esau I hated, and I appointed his borders for desolation and his inheritance for gifts of the wilderness."
verses.1:4: Because one will say, "Idumea has been overthrown, and let us return and rebuild the desolate places," this is what the Lord Almighty says: "They will build, and I will overthrow; and they will be called borders of lawlessness, and a people against whom the Lord stands arrayed forever.
verses.1:5: And your eyes will see, and you yourselves will say, 'The Lord has been magnified above the borders of Israel.'"
verses.1:6: "A son honors a father, and a servant his master. And if I am a father, where is My honor? And if I am a master, where is the fear of Me?" says the Lord Almighty. "You priests who despise My name—yet you said, 'In what way have we despised Your name?'
verses.1:7: By offering defiled loaves at My altar. Yet you said, 'In what way have we defiled them?' By your saying, 'The table of the Lord is defiled,' and you have held in contempt the things placed upon it.
verses.1:8: For if you offer a blind animal for a sacrifice, is it not evil? And if you offer a lame or sick one, is it not evil? Offer it now to your governor: will he accept you? Will he show you favor?" says the Lord Almighty.
verses.1:9: "And now, entreat the face of your God and plead with Him! By your hands these things have happened; will I show favor to any of you?" says the Lord Almighty.
verses.1:10: "Because even among you doors will be shut, and My altar will not be kindled in vain. I have no pleasure in you," says the Lord Almighty, "and I will not accept a sacrifice from your hands.
verses.1:11: For from the rising of the sun even to its setting, My name has been glorified among the nations, and in every place incense is offered to My name, and a pure sacrifice; for My name is great among the nations," says the Lord Almighty.
verses.1:12: "But you profane it by your saying, 'The table of the Lord is defiled,' and the things placed upon it, His foods, are held in contempt.
verses.1:13: And you said, 'These things are from hardship.' And I blew them away," says the Lord Almighty. "And you were bringing in stolen things and the lame and the afflicted; and if you bring the sacrifice, will I accept them from your hands?" says the Lord Almighty.
verses.1:14: "And cursed is the one who was able, and there was a male in his flock, and his vow was upon it, yet he sacrifices a marred one to the Lord. For I am a great King," says the Lord Almighty, "and My name is illustrious among the nations."
verses.2:1: "And now this command is for you, priests.
verses.2:2: If you do not listen, and if you do not lay it to your heart to give glory to My name," says the Lord Almighty, "then I will send out the curse upon you, and I will curse your blessing, and I will curse it; and I will scatter your blessing, and it will not be among you, because you yourselves do not lay it to your heart.
verses.2:3: Look, I am separating the shoulder from you, and I will scatter offal upon your faces, offal of festivals, and I will take you to the same place;
verses.2:4: and you will know that I have sent out this command to you, so that My covenant may be with the Levites," says the Lord Almighty.
verses.2:5: "My covenant with him was one of life and peace, and I granted him to fear with reverence and to stand in awe before My name.
verses.2:6: A law of truth was in his mouth, and injustice was not found on his lips; in peace, keeping a straight course, he walked with Me, and he turned many back from injustice.
verses.2:7: For the lips of a priest will guard knowledge, and they will seek out the law from his mouth, because he is a messenger of the Lord Almighty.
verses.2:8: But you turned aside from the way and weakened many in the law; have you corrupted the covenant of Levi?" says the Lord Almighty.
verses.2:9: "And I also have given you over, held in contempt and cast aside, among all the nations, because you yourselves do not keep My ways, but were showing favoritism in the law."
verses.2:10: Did not one God create you? Is there not one Father of you all? Why is it that you have abandoned, each one his brother, so as to profane the covenant of your fathers?
verses.2:11: Judah has been abandoned, and an abomination has occurred in Israel and in Jerusalem, because Judah profaned the holy things of the Lord, in that he loved and pursued foreign gods.
verses.2:12: The Lord will utterly destroy the man who does these things, until he is even humbled from the tents of Jacob and from among those who offer a sacrifice to the Lord Almighty.
verses.2:13: "And these things which I hated, you were doing: you were covering the altar of the Lord with tears, and with weeping and groaning from toils. Is it still worthy to look upon a sacrifice or to receive what is acceptable from your hands?
verses.2:14: Yet you said, 'For what reason?' Because the Lord testified between you and the wife of your youth, whom you abandoned; and she is your companion and the wife of your covenant.
verses.2:15: And did He not make what is good, and a remnant of His spirit? And you said, 'What else but offspring does God seek?' So guard yourselves in your spirit, and do not abandon the wife of your youth.
verses.2:16: But if you hate her and send her away," says the Lord God of Israel, "then ungodliness will cover over your thoughts," says the Lord Almighty. "So guard yourselves in your spirit, and by no means abandon her,
verses.2:17: you who provoke God with your words. Yet you said, 'In what way have we provoked Him?' By your saying, 'Everyone who does evil is good before the Lord, and in them He Himself is well pleased,' and, 'Where is the God of righteousness?'"
verses.3:1: "Look, I am sending out My messenger, and he will survey a way before Me; and suddenly the Lord whom you seek will come to His own temple, and the messenger of the covenant whom you desire; look, He is coming," says the Lord Almighty.
verses.3:2: And who will endure the day of His entrance? Or who will stand firm at His appearing? For He enters like the fire of a smelting furnace and like the soap-herb of launderers.
verses.3:3: He will sit smelting and purifying as with silver and as with gold, and He will purify the sons of Levi and cast them like gold and like silver; and they will be offering a sacrifice to the Lord in righteousness,
verses.3:4: and the sacrifice of Judah and Jerusalem will please the Lord, just as in the days of old and just as in the former years.
verses.3:5: "And I will draw near to you in judgment, and I will be a swift witness against the sorceresses and against the adulteresses, and against those who swear by My name falsely, and against those who defraud a hired worker of wages, and those who oppress a widow, and those who beat orphans, and those who turn aside the justice of a proselyte, and those who do not fear Me," says the Lord Almighty.
verses.3:6: "For I am the Lord your God, and I have not changed."
verses.3:7: "And you, sons of Jacob, do not refrain from the injustices of your fathers; you have turned aside from My statutes and have not kept them. Return to Me, and I will return to you," says the Lord Almighty. "Yet you said, 'In what way shall we return?'
verses.3:8: Will a human cheat God? For you are cheating Me! And you will say, 'In what way have we cheated You?' Because the tithes and the firstfruits are with you;
verses.3:9: and looking away, you look away, and Me you are cheating.
verses.3:10: The year has been completed, and you brought all the produce into the storehouses, and his plunder will be in his house. Examine now in this," says the Lord Almighty, "whether I will not open for you the floodgates of heaven and pour out My blessing for you until it is enough;
verses.3:11: and I will appoint for you for food, and I will by no means destroy the fruit of your land, and your vine in the field will by no means grow weak," says the Lord Almighty.
verses.3:12: "And all the nations will call you blessed, because you yourselves will be a desirable land," says the Lord Almighty.
verses.3:13: "You have made your words heavy against Me," says the Lord. "Yet you said, 'In what way have we spoken against You?'
verses.3:14: You said, 'Futile is the one who serves God, and what advantage is it that we kept His charges, and that we walked as suppliants before the Lord Almighty?
verses.3:15: And now we ourselves call foreigners blessed, and all who do lawless things are built up, and they opposed God and were saved.'"
verses.3:16: Those who fear the Lord spoke these things, each to his neighbor; and the Lord paid attention and listened, and He wrote a book of remembrance before Himself for those who fear the Lord and who revere His name.
verses.3:17: "And they will be Mine," says the Lord Almighty, "for the day that I am making, as a treasured possession, and I will choose them in the way a man chooses his son who serves him.
verses.3:18: And you will return and see between a righteous person and a lawless person, and between the one who serves God and the one who does not serve.
verses.3:19: For look, a day is coming, burning like an oven, and it will set them ablaze, and all the foreigners and all who do lawless things will be stubble, and the coming day will kindle them," says the Lord Almighty, "and neither root nor branch will by any means be left from them.
verses.3:20: And for you who fear My name, the sun of righteousness will rise, and healing will be in its wings; and you will go out and leap like young calves released from bonds.
verses.3:21: And you will trample down lawless ones, for they will be ashes beneath your feet on the day that I am making," says the Lord Almighty.
verses.3:22: "And look, I am sending to you Elijah the Tishbite before the great and illustrious day of the Lord comes,
verses.3:23: who will restore the heart of a father to a son, and the heart of a person to his neighbor, so that I do not come and strike the land utterly."
verses.3:24: "Remember the law of Moses My servant, just as I commanded him at Horeb for all Israel, decrees and ordinances."

notes.1:1: The Greek reads 'by the hand of His messenger' (rendering Hebrew Malachi as a common noun rather than a proper name) and includes the closing exhortation 'Lay it now upon your hearts,' which is absent from the Hebrew MT.
notes.1:3: The Greek reads 'his borders' (horia) rather than Hebrew 'his mountains,' and 'for gifts of the wilderness' (domata) rather than Hebrew 'for jackals of the wilderness.'
notes.1:4: Idumea (Idoumaia) is the Greek name for Edom; here the Greek makes Idumea the subject of the passive verb 'has been overthrown,' contrasting with the Hebrew first-person plural 'Edom says, We have been shattered.'
notes.1:10: Whereas the Hebrew expresses a wish ('Oh that one among you would shut the doors'), the Greek states a future passive prediction: 'doors will be shut, and My altar will not be kindled in vain.'
notes.1:13: The Greek reads the first-person singular 'I blew them away' (exephysesa), whereas the Hebrew has the second-person plural 'you sniffed at it.'
notes.2:3: Instead of Hebrew 'rebuke your offspring,' the Greek reads 'separating the shoulder from you' and uses enystron ('offal,' specifically the fourth stomach or maw of a sacrificial animal), echoing the priestly portions in Deuteronomy 18:3. The closing verb is also first-person singular ('I will take you to the same place').
notes.2:11: The Greek opens with a passive verb ('Judah has been abandoned,' vs. Hebrew 'Judah has been faithless') and reads 'foreign gods' without the Hebrew phrase 'daughter of a foreign god.' In 2:12, 'until he is even humbled' likewise diverges from the Hebrew idiom 'awake and answering.'
notes.2:15: A notoriously difficult verse; the Greek text translated here reads 'make what is good' (kalon epoiesen, where some Greek witnesses read 'another' and the Hebrew has 'one') and introduces the following question with 'And you said.'
notes.2:16: The Greek frames the opening as a conditional ('if you hate her and send her away,' contrasting with the common translation of the Hebrew as 'I hate divorce') and reads 'ungodliness will cover over your thoughts' instead of Hebrew 'violence on his garment.'
notes.3:1: The Greek verb epiblepsetai means 'will survey' or 'will inspect' rather than Hebrew 'will clear/prepare' the way.
notes.3:5: The first two nouns in the Greek list are feminine plural ('the sorceresses and ... the adulteresses'), whereas the Hebrew has masculine plural forms; the Greek also specifies swearing 'by My name.'
notes.3:8: The Greek verb pternizo ('cheat,' literally 'trip by the heel' or 'supplant,' echoing Jacob in Genesis 27:36) replaces Hebrew 'rob,' and 3:9 reads 'looking away, you look away' instead of Hebrew 'you are cursed with a curse.'
notes.3:10: The Greek diverges substantially from the Hebrew here and in 3:11: 3:10 opens with declarative past actions ('The year has been completed, and you brought all the produce into the storehouses, and his plunder will be in his house'), and 3:11 reads 'I will appoint for you for food, and I will by no means destroy' (first-person singular) instead of Hebrew 'I will rebuke the devourer ... so that it will not destroy.'
notes.3:24: In the Septuagint order, the command to remember Moses' law stands last (3:24) after the Elijah prophecy (3:22-23), reversing the order of the Hebrew MT (3:22-24 / English 4:4-6). The Greek also specifies 'Elijah the Tishbite' (3:22, vs. Hebrew 'the prophet') and 'the heart of a person to his neighbor' (3:23, vs. Hebrew 'the hearts of children to their fathers').
